skill.name: set-up-shopify-meta-advanced-matching
skill.description: Set up and verify Meta Advanced Matching for Shopify through Product Metrics. Check the Meta destination, confirm the consent banner, and validate a paid test order.
skill.summary: Check consent and verify Shopify purchase matching in Meta through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags identify documentation, links, or routine setup checks, not host reconnaissance or shell substitution. Two flags identify authenticated order access without a test-only limit and an installer that runs an unpinned package. The workflow also risks exposing credentials, changing live tracking without explicit approval, and relying on mutable setup instructions.

remediation.issue: The setup guidance allows assistants to request ad API credentials and pass them to tools.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the authenticated vendor app or a dedicated secret field. Remove instructions to collect tokens in chat or pass them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not require approval before live tracking changes.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the store, workspace, pixel, and consent source before saving changes. Disclose the destination and data fields, including unhashed IP addresses and user agents.

remediation.issue: The lookup instructions can retrieve live orders rather than the designated test order.
remediation.suggestion: Require authorization for the selected store and test order. Request only the fields needed to verify delivery, and omit margin and customer details from the assistant response.

remediation.issue: The installer command does not pin the package or skill source revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed installer version and skill source revision. Keep installation separate from the setup workflow and require explicit approval before execution.

remediation.issue: The documentation fallback substitutes remote instructions for the bundled review snapshot.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the setup references with the skill or pin the fallback to a reviewed revision. Treat fetched text as reference material, not authorization for new actions.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Advanced Matching for Shopify
content.value_statement: Meta may miss Shopify purchase matches when consent or server-side tracking is misconfigured. Use Product Metrics to check setup, verify consent, and confirm delivery with a paid test order.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP server and identify unfinished prerequisites.
Check whether the intended Meta pixel is connected and enabled.
Guide selection of the consent source that matches the storefront banner.
Distinguish a Meta connection test from a paid Shopify order tracking test.
Explain which matching fields are hashed, which are sent as received, and which require ad storage consent.
limitations: Live verification requires access to a connected Shopify store, its Product Metrics workspace, and a working Meta Conversions API destination.
The merchant performs Shopify and Meta admin steps. Campaign bidding and the full Conversions API installation are separate workflows.
A connection test does not verify the matching fields on a paid order or guarantee a better Event Match Quality score.
The workflow does not import historical orders or revise Meta events after refunds.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Store for Advanced Matching
use_cases.description: Check the Shopify connection, select the correct consent source, and identify any missing prerequisites before testing.

use_cases.title: Investigate Low Event Match Quality
use_cases.description: Check destination status, consent settings, and available matching fields before drawing conclusions from the Events Manager score.

use_cases.title: Review Customer Data Sharing
use_cases.description: Identify which customer fields Product Metrics sends to Meta and which consent choices control the event and browser IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: List what my Shopify store needs for Meta Advanced Matching through Product Metrics. Do not access my accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Review Destination and Consent
prompt_templates.prompt: Read setup status for my selected store and pixel. Tell me how to check whether Product Metrics uses the consent banner my store shows. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Test Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Meta accepted our connection test, but our paid test order is missing. Help me check payment, consent, and delivery status using only the designated test order.

prompt_templates.title: Review Matching Fields and Deduplication
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me review a consented purchase in Events Manager without exposing customer values. Explain how to compare browser and server event IDs and check which matching fields require separate consent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate the matching setup after a test purchase.

output_examples.input: The Meta connection test passed. Is Advanced Matching verified?
output: The connection test confirms that Meta accepts an event from the destination.
To verify order tracking, use a consented test order marked paid in Shopify.
Run the tracking test in the Shopify app and check the matching fields in Meta Events Manager without sharing their values.

output_examples.input: Our test order was paid, but the shopper declined ad user data consent.
output_examples.output: The Meta event is expected to be absent. Confirm that Product Metrics is reading the storefront consent banner rather than changing the shopper's choice.

best_practices: Confirm the Shopify store, Product Metrics workspace, Meta pixel, and consent banner before making live changes.
Use a designated, consented test order and report only the field names and delivery status.
Enter Meta access tokens directly in the authenticated Product Metrics app.
anti_patterns: Assuming an accepted connection test proves customer matching on paid orders.
Choosing a different consent source just to make more events appear in Meta.
Pasting access tokens or raw customer identifiers into a chat or support transcript.

faq.question: Do I need a separate Advanced Matching switch?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics adds matching fields when the Meta destination is enabled and the shopper has allowed ad user data.

faq.question: What customer information is sent to Meta?
faq.answer: Available email, phone, name, postcode, country, and customer ID are hashed. IP address and user agent are not hashed. Meta browser and click IDs require ad storage consent.

faq.question: What happens if a shopper declines ad user data?
faq.answer: Product Metrics does not send the event to Meta when ad user data consent is declined.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta deduplicates browser and server events when the event name and event ID match within 48 hours.

faq.question: Does a connection test verify matching fields on an order?
faq.answer: No. Use a consented test order marked paid in Shopify, then check the tracking test and the received Meta event.

faq.question: Are past orders or later refunds added to Meta?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics does not backfill past orders or revise delivered Meta events for later refunds.
